title: So I commanded Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 to make games each with different genre. Each chat is working in one. Is it a good idea? It doesn't seem so.
author: Need300dollars
selftext: So I just tell AI to do games. I picked one 3D mobile game so they have reference and tell them some things so every one of them have in common (like the game will be published in Google Play), each one in separate chat. Would it come out good? One of them already came with a game where character had the sword in his shoulder and animation was just an horizontal slash. I though Opus 5.5 would do triple A animation, but just give me one A. Can they actually do good animation or is it just scam and lies that vibe coders post here?

comments.author: Kavrae
comments.body: No.  Even when using AI as a tool (note : tool, not replacement), put some effort and pride into your development.

replies.author: Need300dollars
replies.body: I put it giving more prompts. I can't do much because I only have a phone. Vibe coding is the only way for me toget stuff (and pirating).

comments.author: youwishyouwhereme1
comments.body: Have you heard about fantasy? I hope you really rage-baiting

replies.author: mirageofstars
replies.body: I actually think OP is being serious

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: AI can automate and do things fast, but if you are trying to create anything in AI, distributing yourself across so many apps seems like a dilution of effort. You'll end up with 18 meh things instead of one or two promising things.

comments.author: thecrustycrap
comments.body: same energy as claude make me a million mrr saas, no mistakes

comments.author: mechatui
comments.body:
Yea you can create replicated games quite easily and produce slop that you can throw onto the App Store with minimal effort

Just don’t expect other game developers to respect you

replies.author: Ichi_Wang
replies.body: i'm just going off a hunch here but something tells me OP isn't looking for respect

comments.author: sumdeadhorse
comments.body: Slop like this gives Aigamedev a bad name

comments.author: Need300dollars
comments.body: So everyone will just say "put effort" which means do better prompts. I only have my phone to work with and nobody answer the question like they ask for effort but don't help. I will say thank you but please say something more. Is it a prompt that specifically calls animation details?

replies.author: Kavrae
replies.body: Stop focusing on prompts. Move away from AI. Use that phone to learn how games are built. Come back when you know what to make, why, and how to test it.

replies.author: Need300dollars
replies.body: I already learned it. But working from phone is super hard and laggy (my phone is a Samsung A21s). Thank you anyways.

replies.author: davidbabinec
replies.body: Effort means your own vision, idea you could write a book about. Making a good product requires clear vision, polish and understanding of it. If the AI is doing 18 games for you I doubt that you can explain mechanics of any of them, as AI is just having a non stop party there. Pick one thing, and put your maximum into it. Read every response it gives you, test all the time, and improve on every little detail, otherwise it will be sloppy slop..

replies.author: Need300dollars
replies.body: Thank you, but, what prompt would you make so it makes better animation? Don't tell me "that's your job" because I came here to ask for help. I'm already putting my effort, what would you know? Help with what I asked so I can thank you.

comments.author: davidbabinec
comments.body: Have you tried hooking up Claude to your printer? It can immediately start printing money! But seriously, save up the $25 fee for Google Play, this will not work unless you put a huge effort and quality from yourself.

comments.author: Need300dollars
comments.body:
Thanks to everyone who commented. I think my original post wasn't clear about what I need, so let me be more specific. 
I'm not looking for general advice on effort or motivation. I'm looking for a technical way to get AI to produce better character animation. 
If you've gotten good animation out of AI, even once, what prompt structure, tool, or workflow worked for you? Even a single tip would help a lot.
